title: Make a grayscale image
summary: Grayscale stores one brightness value per pixel. It drops colour detail while keeping a brightness view useful for some image operations.
introduction: Grayscale stores one brightness value per pixel. It drops colour detail while keeping a brightness view useful for some image operations. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Grayscale stores one brightness value per pixel. It drops colour detail while keeping a brightness view useful for some image operations.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

bgr = np.full((2, 3, 3), 100, dtype=np.uint8)
gray = cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
print(gray.shape, gray[0, 0].item())
blocks.title: Make a grayscale image

blocks.text: The output is (2, 3) 100. Equal BGR values of 100 become a gray value of 100. The result has no three-channel dimension.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Grayscale conversion is not simply taking the blue channel for every coloured pixel.
For more detail later, use this [OpenCV further reading](https://docs.opencv.org/4.x/d6/d00/tutorial_py_root.html).
